text: On the night of April the twenty-sixth, nineteen eighty-six, the crew was running a safety test, to see if a spinning-down turbine could keep the water pumps going during a blackout. The test had been delayed by about ten hours, and handed to the night shift. Power fell far too low, and the reactor was choked by xenon, a by-product that also swallows neutrons. To push the power back up, the operators pulled out almost all the control rods. Far more than the rules allowed. Then the test began. As the turbine slowed, the pumps slowed, less water flowed, and more of it boiled.
